summary: Added orphaned pipeline rollback to the stage node factory. When `ledger_begin_work` is called by the Deep Agent before the stage crashes, the error handler automatically calls `ledger_cancel_pipeline` with `auto_cancelled=True` and `reason='Orchestrator stage error: ...'`, preventing the orphaned IN_PROGRESS pipeline from blocking the next run attempt. Implementation: (1) `_STAGE_PIPELINE_TYPE` map at module level for stage→pipeline-type lookup; (2) `_install_begin_work_tracker` wraps `ledger_begin_work.ainvoke` to set a mutable tracker dict; (3) `_begin_work_state` and `wrapped_tools` declared before `try` for except-block access; (4) rollback logic in except with graceful failure handling (logs WARNING, preserves original error). Added 4 unit tests covering: rollback called after begin_work+crash, not called without begin_work, run_log contains pipeline_rollback entry, original error preserved when cancel fails. All 525 tests pass (9 graph.py failures are pre-existing).

comments.note: The `_STAGE_PIPELINE_TYPE` map covers 6 stages (developer, qa, reviewer, docs, security_auditor, release_engineer). The `pm` and `synthesis` stages intentionally have no entry because they never call `ledger_begin_work`. If a new stage is added that calls begin_work, the map must be updated. Consider adding a test that asserts `_STAGE_PIPELINE_TYPE` covers all WP-scoped stages, to prevent future drift.

The `_install_begin_work_tracker` uses a separate `_orig_ainvoke_bw` sentinel to avoid colliding with the `_orig_ainvoke` (inject_project_path) and `_orig_ainvoke_wp` (restrict_to_wp) sentinels. This three-sentinel pattern is clean but may become a maintenance burden if more wrappers are added. A registry or single-wrapper composition approach could unify all wrappers in a future refactor.

comments.note: ACs 1-6 NOT IMPLEMENTED — supervisor.py has zero code to cancel halted WPs. The circuit breaker at line 543 correctly detects WPs with >=3 consecutive failures and skips them with a `halted_repeated_failure` log entry, but never calls `ledger_update_work_package_status` (or any MCP tool) to transition those WPs to CANCELLED. When all WPs are halted, the loop exhausts and falls through to the 'all roles returned WAIT/skip → synthesis' catch-all path. The WPs remain IN_PROGRESS in the ledger, violating §19.1's precondition that all WPs must be terminal before synthesis can run. Developer must add supervisor-level cancellation logic before routing to synthesis.

AC2 gap: Synthesis is dispatched via the 'all roles returned WAIT/skip' fallback (reason='all roles returned WAIT'), not through a dedicated 'all WPs terminal' guard triggered by explicit cancellation. The 'all WPs terminal (COMPLETE or CANCELLED)' guard at line 480 would only fire AFTER the WPs are transitioned to CANCELLED — but since cancellation never happens, this guard is never reached in the halted scenario. Both the MCP tool call for cancellation and the synthesis dispatch sequence are missing.

AC6 gap: No unit tests exist for the halted-WP cancellation + synthesis dispatch flow. Grep of orchestrator/tests/ confirms zero tests reference the 'Cancelled: exceeded orchestrator failure threshold' reason string or the cancellation path in supervisor.py.

AC10 minor observation: when rollback itself fails, `log.warning()` is correctly emitted to Python logging (satisfying the AC) but the failure is NOT streamed to the JSONL run_log via `run_logger.stream_entry()`. The run_log will have no trace of the rollback failure, only the original stage_error entry. This is observable only via Python process logs. Consider adding a rollback_fail entry to run_log for better end-to-end observability, but this does not block QA pass/fail for this AC as written.

ACs 7-12 (nodes rollback) are fully implemented and verified. All 4 new TestPipelineRollback tests pass: rollback_called_when_begin_work_invoked_before_error, rollback_not_called_when_begin_work_not_invoked, rollback_run_log_contains_pipeline_rollback_entry, rollback_original_error_preserved_when_cancel_fails. 521 orchestrator tests pass (excluding 9 pre-existing test_graph.py failures unrelated to this WP).

summary: PASS. Two interrelated features implemented cleanly and minimally. (1) supervisor.py halted-WP cancellation loop: iterates wp_summaries after all roles return WAIT, calls ledger_update_work_package_status(CANCELLED, agent='Project Manager') for each non-terminal WP at the 3-failure threshold, logs WARNING + halted_wp_cancelled run_log entry per WP, swallows cancellation errors gracefully, then routes to synthesis. (2) nodes/__init__.py pipeline rollback: _install_begin_work_tracker wraps ledger_begin_work.ainvoke to set a _begin_work_state dict; the except block uses this to auto-cancel any orphaned IN_PROGRESS pipeline with auto_cancelled=True, logs a pipeline_rollback INFO entry, and preserves the original error if cancel itself fails. Architecture strengths: three-sentinel wrapper pattern (_orig_ainvoke, _orig_ainvoke_wp, _orig_ainvoke_bw) is clean and follows established conventions; _RecordingTool test stub avoids MagicMock attribute auto-creation which would break hasattr sentinel checks; WP_TERMINAL_STATUSES extracted to config.py (proactive cleanup). Tests are comprehensive: 9 new tests across two classes, all exercising real code paths. One documentation-forward gap: two new log entry types not yet in architecture.md JSONL table.
